mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% for two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% coincident with a drop in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 10% month-over-month indicates weakening aggregate demand, which depresses corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the unemployment rate above 6% for three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, reducing consumer spending and corporate profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 60% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average by more than 3% for two consecutive months indicates supply-side stress, which typically precedes negative equity returns as profit margins erode over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 12-mo MA by >3% for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 55% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid increase in payroll employment (PAYEMS) of more than 400,000 persons in a single month, combined with a concurrent decline in the unemployment rate by more than 0.5 percentage points, signals a tight labor market that increases wage pressure and cost of capital, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +1%) in at least 60% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in the federal funds rate below 1% for three consecutive months signals an accommodative monetary policy stance, which typically supports risk asset valuations and results in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +1%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A month-over-month increase in real personal savings (RSAFS) by more than 5% coincident with a decline in personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) by more than 1% suggests households are saving rather than spending, which typically precedes negative equity returns as demand weakens over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 55% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in industrial production (INDPRO) above its 12-month moving average by more than 2% for four consecutive months signals improving supply conditions and expanding economic activity, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO > 12-mo MA by >2% for 4 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +1%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.
